title: Assessment of Skills of Caregivers Providing Care for Stroke Patients in East Kazakhstan Region
content:
Objectives: This study investigated the lives of people after stroke and the characteristics of care management after discharge from hospital to home. The study aimed to identify caregiving difficulties and to assess mastery of skills in implementing recovery activities at home. 
Study design: This was a cross-sectional study. 
Methods: As part of the study, we interviewed 205 relatives caring for stroke survivors. Descriptive statistics: frequencies, mean, medians, standard deviations were calculated. 
Results: Caregivers determined that the main actions are aimed at restoring motor activity 58% (p≤0.021) and the difficulties they most often encounter during caregiving are difficulties related to obtaining information from medical personnel, or not understanding the information received in persons under 50 years of age was 47.9%, while in persons over 50 years of age this indicator was 49.5%. The emotional state of the relative is closely interrelated with the state of the patient. Persons with higher education are more resistant to these changes related to the patient's health. 
Conclusion:The results of this study provide a focus on the essentials of home care and will help improve patient safety and reduce re-hospitalizations in this population, which in turn will improve the effectiveness of informal care.
